newsitem.title: USA: Caliber says losses at Viking hurt Q3.
newsitem.headline: Caliber says losses at Viking hurt Q3.

text.p: Caliber System Inc said on Monday its third quarter 1996 losses were due to ongoing losses at its Viking Freight unit and lower-than-expected volume growth at its small package carrier.

"We anticipate a profitable fourth quarter, although, as announced on July 1, we will finish the year with 1996 results significantly below those of 1995," Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Daniel Sullivan said.
Caliber earlier reported an operating loss of $0.05 per share in the third quarter 1996 against a $0.56 per share profit in the same period last year.

Caliber, which was trying to combine its four regional carriers into one large carrier called Viking Freight, said expenses and one-time costs related to the consolidation hurt operations in the quarter.
Aggressive industry-wide discounting and higher fuel prices also had a negative impact, Caliber said.
"The cost overruns this year are clearly unacceptable," Sullivan said.

"In addition to the external forces of a very competitive industry, the situation at Viking is the result of several internal issues caused by significant tonnage growth during the process of consoidation and operations ability to repsond on a nationwide basis," he said.
Sullivan said Caliber had consequently begun a major study of the company's terminal and linehaul operations.
Viking had also implemented an aggressive strategy to increase revenues and eliminate unprofitable businesses, Sullivan said.
Viking was also trying to finish its consolidation as quickly and efficiently as possible because of the associated costs, he said.

"On a positive note, many accounts have accepted discount reductions and chosen to keep their businesses with Viking," Sullivan said. "Viking also announced a 5.9 percent rate increase, effective September 16, 1996."

Lower volume growth at the company's small package carrier, RPS, also hurt quarterly results, Caliber said. A sluggish retail sector, an aggressive pricing environment and increased fixed costs also had a negative impact, it said.

"Investment in non-critical programs and products is being reevaluated and reduced or eliminated if appropriate," Sullivan said. "A number of RPS headquarters positions have been eliminated commensurate with the reduction in workload."
